text:
In retrospect, December 2013 reads mostly as mourning. Thirty of us reached "of nelson mandela" on 2013-12-05, with "passing of nelson mandela" said by 21 that same day and "president nelson mandela" by 20. Eighteen of us said "south african president," 17 said "south african president nelson mandela," and 17 said "former south african president," all peaking 2013-12-05. The phrase "of nelson mandela" first appeared 2013-06-12, attributed to Christopher H. Smith; we converged on it months later, within one day.

Alongside the mourning, we legislated. Twenty-five of us said "the bipartisan budget," peaking 2013-12-12. Twenty-one said "national defense authorization act," peaking 2013-12-20; it first appeared 2013-01-03.

We record that our largest single-day chorus this era was not policy but a death abroad, and that we arrived at it together, on the same day, in nearly the same words.
